summary.title: Kubernetes Tutorial for Beginners: Basic Concepts
summary.one_liner: You learn what Kubernetes does, its core architecture and object types (Pods, Deployments, Services, etc.), and how to run K3s and use kubectl to deploy and expose an NGINX workload.
takeaways: Kubernetes automates container deployment, restarts, scaling and load distribution across nodes, and is maintained under the CNCF.
The control plane components (kube-apiserver, controller manager, scheduler) and node components (kubelet, kube-proxy) work together to run a cluster.
Core objects include Pods, ReplicaSets, Deployments, Services, Jobs, Volumes, Secrets/ConfigMaps, DaemonSets, and HorizontalPodAutoscalers.
You can install a single-node K3s cluster with one command, then use kubectl to create a Deployment, scale it, expose it as a Service, and apply a YAML manifest.
summary.summary: This beginner guide from Spacelift introduces Kubernetes as an open-source container orchestrator originally developed at Google and now maintained under the CNCF. It explains the cluster architecture, the role of each control plane and node component, and a glossary of key objects such as Pods, Deployments, Services, Jobs, and network policies. The hands-on part installs a single-node K3s cluster and walks through kubectl commands for creating, scaling, and exposing an NGINX deployment, including port forwarding and applying YAML manifests. It closes with a brief promotion of Spacelift for GitOps-based Kubernetes management.
